input.quote: This is IBM's entire obligation to Customer with regard to any claim of infringement.
input.rationale: Section 8.1 gives an IP infringement indemnity only (Materials/Base Components), with usual exclusions and procure/modify/replace/credit remedies — this meets the fallback but not the preferred position, which also requires vendor indemnities for breach of applicable law, security incidents affecting Customer data and gross negligence/wilful misconduct. Conversely, Customer's indemnity in 8.2 is broader than the playbook allows: item 3 covers any Services Recipient claim relating directly or indirectly to IBM's own Services, a one-way indemnity for Vendor's services (walk-away territory), only partially offset by the carve-back in 8.2(c). Redline adds the vendor misconduct prongs after the 8.1 exclusions (clarifying that the "entire obligation" sole-remedy language applies only to infringement claims) and narrows 8.2(3) to Customer's breach of applicable law, leaving Content/AUP and mechanics' lien prongs intact.

proposal.summary: Add IBM indemnity for breach of law, Content security incidents and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; narrow Customer's indemnity from all Services Recipient claims to Customer's breach of law.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] Section 8.1 covers only IP infringement, so we have added IBM's indemnity for its breach of law, unauthorized access to Content caused by IBM, and its gross negligence or wilful misconduct, consistent with our position that the vendor stands behind its own misconduct. We have also narrowed our indemnity in 8.2, which currently covers any Services Recipient claim relating directly or indirectly to IBM's own Services, to our Content and our breach of law; if helpful, we can discuss a super-cap on IBM's indemnity as a fallback.

ops.text: In addition to and without limiting IBM's obligations set forth above, IBM will defend, indemnify and hold harmless Customer, its Enterprise and their respective employees, officers, agents and directors from and against any third party claim, and all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees), to the extent arising out of (i) IBM's breach of applicable law; (ii) any unauthorized access to, use or disclosure of Content caused by IBM or its Subcontractors; or (iii) IBM's gross negligence or willful misconduct. The statement above that indemnification is IBM's entire obligation applies solely to claims of infringement and does not limit this paragraph.
